logline: A socially awkward British teen sets up an underground sex therapy clinic with his classmate, drawing on his mother's expertise as a sex therapist to navigate his peers' most intimate anxieties.

bollymeter.basis: 91 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 80 reviews; critics praised its warmth, honest treatment of teen sexuality, and Asa Butterfield and Emma Mackey's chemistry.

pull_quotes.text: The season develops in tone and depth beyond its initial easy comic setup, validating teenagers' problems as real.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 launched in January 2019 and landed at 91 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 80 critics. The premise, socially awkward Otis Milburn running a sex-advice clinic out of a school toilet while navigating his own anxieties, gives the show a conceptual hook. The writing leans into the warmth of its ensemble and avoids mocking its characters for their inexperience. The show’s comedy carries genuine depth beneath its surface setup. Its 8-episode first run establishes an Americana-inflected British school setting that becomes the series signature aesthetic.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Sex Education's premiere establishes its tonal argument in the opening minutes: a graphic sex scene, immediately followed by its emotional aftermath, and a conversation about whether what just happened was any good. Gillian Anderson's Jean Milburn and Asa Butterfield's Otis arrive as a mother-son dynamic that is simultaneously the show's most original element and its structural engine.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Otis giving his first piece of sex advice to Jackson on the rugby field - the scene that establishes his ability and his discomfort with it, and that sets the series' entire premise in motion.
episode_reviews.review_body: The Sex Education premiere earned the show its 91% Rotten Tomatoes debut score through its commitment to the uncomfortable gap between what sex looks like and what it costs people emotionally. The Moordale High setting - a British school that aesthetically references American 1980s teen cinema - creates the kind of deliberate anachronism that frees the show from period specificity while anchoring it in familiar archetypes. Asa Butterfield's Otis is the series' moral centre: a boy who understands the theory of intimacy through his therapist mother's practice but has no practical experience of his own. Emma Mackey's Maeve completes the pilot equation - a character whose edge and intelligence make the Otis partnership immediately worth watching.

bollymeter.basis: 98 percent from 57 critics on Rotten Tomatoes; season 2 deepened its ensemble and broadened its emotional register, with Aimee Lou Wood's storyline drawing particular critical attention.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 dropped in January 2020 and earned strong critical approval, landing 98 percent from 57 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes. The show grows in confidence, with a deeper ensemble, higher emotional stakes, and a subplot involving Aimee Lou Wood's character addressing sexual assault handled without sensationalism. Wood's performance earned her a BAFTA for Best Female Comedy Performance. The season also uses its expanded canvas to give secondary characters room to breathe, moving beyond the central Otis-Maeve dynamic to build a fuller community portrait. The broadening stands out as the season's main strength.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 deepened the ensemble rather than simply escalating the central romance, earning the show its strongest critical reception to that point.

bollymeter.basis: 98 percent from 42 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes; won Best Comedy Series at the 50th International Emmy Awards.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 arrived in September 2021 and matched season 2's 98-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 42 reviews, then went on to win Best Comedy Series at the 50th International Emmy Awards in November 2022. The new headmistress character, played by Jemima Kirke, reconfigured the school's power dynamics and gave the season a fresh structural conflict. The ensemble storytelling tightens and the emotional resolution feels more earned than in prior seasons. The International Emmy win reinforces the show's standing as one of the standout British streaming exports of its era.
seasons.season_over_season: A reconfigured school hierarchy and a tighter emotional arc gave season 3 the same critical ceiling as season 2 while adding real structural invention.

bollymeter.basis: 88 percent from 48 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes; critics called it a bittersweet farewell that satisfied emotionally despite relocating the cast to a new school setting that not everyone accepted.

pull_quotes.text: As sweetly empathetic and inclusive as ever, Sex Education's final season serves as a bittersweet but largely satisfying farewell.
There aren't a lot of television shows that make the world a better place by existing. Sex Education is one.

seasons.review_body: The final season landed in September 2023 at 88 percent from 48 reviews on Rotten Tomatoes, a step below the show's peak but still strongly positive. The relocation from Moordale to Cavendish College divided audience response: some welcomed the narrative reset while others felt it disrupted the community-level warmth the show had built. Critics broadly agreed the season handled its send-offs with care, giving major characters satisfying arcs. The Chicago Reader's praise - that the show makes the world better by existing - captured the consensus tone: affectionate, slightly elegiac, aware of what made the series work even if this final run does not quite replicate the heights of seasons 2 and 3.
seasons.season_over_season: A new setting gave the finale season creative room but cost it some of the accumulated warmth of Moordale; critics remained positive while audiences were more divided.
